chains.title: T-favored forkhead-family binding contributes to regulation of TOX3 at the breast-cancer risk locus

links.claim: FOXA1 is expressed and has a ChIP-seq peak over the variant in MCF-7. A FOXA2-mapped QBiC-SELEX model predicts stronger in-vitro binding to T than C at a strong site. This supports a forkhead-family sequence effect, but does not establish FOXA1-specific allele-dependent occupancy. FOXA1 is prioritized over the other candidates partly because the literature search returned a report connecting FOXA1 affinity variation with TOX3 expression at the 16q12.1 risk locus; the masked variant identifier limits confirmation that this is this exact SNP.

The variant lies in distal enhancer-like cCRE EH38E3180851. The reported activity scores are maxima across biosamples, not measurements specific to MCF-7, and the evidence does not establish that this cCRE is the element involved in the literature-reported TOX3 effect.

TOX3 is nearby and strongly prioritized by breast-cancer locus-to-gene analyses. The literature search returned a report describing a risk-locus SNP effect on TOX3 and FOXA1-affinity changes at distal regulatory elements, but the SNP identifier is masked and the evidence does not directly connect EH38E3180851 to TOX3. No significant relevant GTEx eQTL is reported.
MCF-7 is a plausible test context because FOXA1 is expressed and has a ChIP-seq peak over the variant there; neither result establishes allele-specific occupancy.

The variant is strongly associated with breast cancer, and the strongest listed associations identify T as the effect allele, compatible with the predicted T-favored in-vitro binding. A breast-cancer-related association also reports C, and the evidence does not establish FOXA1 mediation of disease risk.

predictions: In heterozygous MCF-7 cells, allele-resolved FOXA1 occupancy should favor T over C if this chain is active; compared with the GATA3 chain, FOXA1 should show the more prominent variant-associated allelic occupancy effect.
Editing C to T should alter enhancer output if the variant is functional, and may alter TOX3 expression; the direction of the expression change is not established.
The proposed route predicts that perturbing EH38E3180851 should affect TOX3 regulation, although the element-to-gene connection remains unproven.
falsified_if: A suitably powered allele-resolved assay in relevant breast cells finds no T-favored FOXA1 occupancy.
Precise variant editing shows no reproducible regulatory effect, or element perturbation and contact or expression assays fail to support a link from EH38E3180851 to TOX3.
